data.summary: Run an AI task that can use configured capabilities, wait for input, and resume on events.

requiredFields.note: Model id, a plain string (the object form is fallbackModel's), naming a model in the company's model catalog.
The prompt, as free prose. Required key, a string or null, and not empty. Termination is never read from its headings: use endFunction.

optionalFields.note: Optional: a string or null. What the engine does with it is not traced in workflow-core.
A company-registered custom model: { name, provider, id?, model? }, outside the model catalog. Its resolution is not traced in workflow-core.
Backup model: { name, provider, model?, id? }. fallbackModel.model names a model in the catalog.
Optional numeric id.
Required inside fallbackModel: the model's name.
Model id from the catalog, resolved with fallbackModel.provider as the explicit provider.
Required inside fallbackModel: the provider name, any string ('' included). Resolves fallbackModel.model against the catalog.
Authoring-only, optional: es | en | pt. Picks the language of the instruction headers and the Cierre / Sesión expirada / error texts. The engine ignores it; say the language in instructions too.
The message the node starts from. Required non-blank on an entry AI_TASK (reached from START or WEBHOOK, no INPUT or CHANNEL_MESSAGE upstream): use '{{$message.text}}'.
Memory key the node's result is stored under, as an object: read it with $memory.getJson in CODE. It takes no whitespace and none of . [ ] $ { }. Empty: the engine uses 'response'.
The capabilities attached to the model: tools, mcp, workflows, function, datum.
Tool entries, each one of four shapes: HTTP (httpToolId), registry (toolkitId), native (external: false) or marketplace. Absent means []; null is kept and fails at run time.
One tool entry, in one of the four shapes.
Entry id: required on registry and marketplace tools, optional on HTTP and native tools. No reader of it is traced in workflow-core.
HTTP tool only, and required there: it marks the entry as an HTTP tool, which must then carry a non-empty description.
Required on every shape: the tool's name. With external: false it must name a native tool.
What the tool does. Required on registry and marketplace tools, and required non-empty on HTTP tools (a schema refinement; whitespace passes); optional on native tools.
HTTP tool only, and required there: the request it makes (url, method, headers, parameters, body, authentication, settings). How the engine applies it is not traced in workflow-core.
After this tool returns: 'none', 'end_function' or 'pause'. What each value does is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional, same values as action: 'none', 'end_function' or 'pause'. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
HTTP and marketplace tools. Anything but false enables the tool: absent, null, 0 and '' all enable it.
HTTP and registry tools: optional parameter values by name, any value. No reader is traced in workflow-core.
HTTP and registry tools: optional mode per parameter name, 'dynamic' or 'static'. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
HTTP and registry tools: optional boolean. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional per-tool boolean, on every shape. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core. The node-wide switch is settings.toonFormat.
Required on native tools, optional on registry, HTTP and marketplace tools. false marks a native tool, whose name must be one of the native tools.
HTTP tools generated from a Datum collection: the source database id. No effect on execution.
HTTP tools generated from a Datum collection: the source database slug. No effect on execution.
HTTP tools generated from a Datum collection: the source database name. No effect on execution.
HTTP tools generated from a Datum collection: the collection name. No effect on execution.
HTTP tools generated from a Datum collection: the operation the request performs. No effect on execution; configuration holds the request.
Registry tools: the required numeric tool id. Marketplace tools: an optional string id.
Registry tools: optional numeric toolkit id.
Tool version: required on registry tools, optional on marketplace tools.
Registry tool only, and required there: its input records. Shape only: no reader of an input record is traced in workflow-core.
Registry tools: optional thumbnail id, an integer or null. No effect on execution.
Native tools (external: false): the operations it may call. Absent falls back to operations; empty or no match allows every known operation.
Native tools (external: false): the older name of allowedOperations, read only when allowedOperations is absent.
Native tools (external: false): { <operation>: { <param>: { mode, value? } } }.
Native tools (external: false): optional list of tag names, each a string. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Native tools (external: false): optional list of field names. With restrictFields true, fields outside it are rejected; otherwise they are only preferred.
Native tools (external: false): true rejects fields outside preferredFields; absent means prefer-only. The engine treats a non-boolean as false.
Native tools (external: false): a namespace for memory keys; omit it for the default (unscoped) one. The engine coerces a non-string to an empty namespace.
Marketplace tools: optional 'marketplace', 'internal' or 'external'. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Marketplace tool only: its input JSON Schema, { name, type: 'object', required?, properties, description }. Shape only: no reader is traced in workflow-core.
Marketplace tools: optional installation id string. Valid here, unlike on a connections.mcp entry, where the key is rejected.
Marketplace tools: optional string. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Marketplace tool only: the selected tool, { id, name, version?, description?, inputParameters?, parameters? }. Shape only: no reader is traced in workflow-core.
Datum connections: [{ id, datumId, name, operations, schema? }]. Absent means none; no reader is traced in workflow-core.
MCP servers the model may use. Absent means []. With any entry, a bare $memory.x in instructions or startCommand reaches the model as literal text: wrap it as {{$memory.x}}.
One server. It needs userAppInstallations with an id; a userAppInstallationId key is rejected here: that key belongs to the standalone MCP node.
Optional server URL. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional marketplace slug of the app (google_calendar, calendly, ...). Recommended: validate recognises a scheduling app by it. No effect on execution.
Optional server name.
Optional server description.
Optional request headers: string values by name.
The installed marketplace apps behind the server: a non-empty list, each with an id.
One installation: { id, name }.
Required and non-blank: the id of an existing marketplace app installation.
Required: the app's name.
Optional icon URL of the app. No effect on execution.
Optional description of the app. No effect on execution.
Optional server-wide disposition: 'none', 'end_function' or 'pause'. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional disposition per tool name, same values as action. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Workflows exposed to the model: [{ name, description, path }]. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Functions exposed to the model: [{ name, headers?, action? }]. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
{ enabled, files }. enabled true with no files takes a model that reads images and PDFs.
Knowledge file records, as a list. Absent or an empty list: the knowledge tool is not registered; a non-empty list registers it. One bare record parses but counts as none.
Model and rendering settings; every key inside it is optional.
Optional model temperature, a number.
How long the node waits: { enabled, duration?, time?, timeInSeconds? }. The engine rounds the window, uses 28800 s when it is not positive, and caps it at 72000 s.
Required. true needs duration and time; false does not mean never: the external agent cache limit applies instead.
Number, or a string the engine renders as a template first. Required with time when enabled is true.
Unit of duration: seconds, minutes, hours or days. Required with duration when enabled is true.
The window in seconds, a number or a string. When positive it takes precedence over duration and time; the engine applies the rounding, default and cap.
Optional boolean. true sets the step up to receive PDFs; it takes a model that reads PDF input.
Optional boolean. true sets the step up to receive images; it takes a model with vision.
Images for the model: [{ name, url }]. Each url is template-interpolated, so {{$memory.*}} works. A non-empty list takes a model with vision.
Optional boolean: whether the model sees a tapped button's hidden payload.
{ enabled, count? }. The engine seeds history only when enabled is exactly true, and count is then required. A count above 15 raises token cost; below 1 is invalid.
Required inside messageHistory. Only true turns it on.
How many messages. Required when enabled is true; above 15 raises token cost, below 1 is invalid.
Optional boolean. What an absent value does at run time is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional boolean. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional boolean. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional boolean; omit it to mean off. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Optional boolean. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Pauses between split bubbles: { enabled?, msPerChar?, minMs?, maxMs?, mediaMs?, fixedMs? }. Enabled needs a value, and applies only with splitMessages true.
Platform context blocks: userInfo, botInfo, companyInfo. Each is a boolean or { enabled, fields?, title? }; both forms are valid, so never rewrite one into the other.
Data-loss-prevention settings. With isDlpEnabled true and no scrubbingRules nothing is redacted; each rule needs a non-empty infoType.
Security guardrails: enabled, preset and modelArmor required; features, thresholds, responseStrategy, userMessaging and performance optional. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
Reminder switch. Absent means false. true without reminder uses the engine's reminder defaults; a reminder without canRemind true is never scheduled.
Optional { timeInSeconds?, times?, remindPrompt? }. Read only when canRemind is true; absent keys take the engine's defaults.
Wait before the first reminder, in seconds. At or past the node's expiration window no reminder is sent.
How many reminders. Absent, an engine constant applies; its value is not in workflow-core.
Optional reminder prompt. Its runtime effect is not traced in workflow-core.
{ enabled, id? }. enabled true requires a non-empty id (whitespace passes). What the agent is is not traced in workflow-core.
Required inside agent: a boolean.
Required and non-empty when enabled is true (a schema refinement; whitespace passes).
How the model ends the conversation: { description, rawSchema? }. Set it with a non-blank description; the schema also accepts null, which means the runtime default.
When the conversation may end and what must be filled first. Required non-blank. Termination is configured here, never inferred from the instructions' headings.
Fields the model hands back: { <field>: { type, description?, required? } }; the engine reads only those three keys. Omitted or empty: the engine default applies.
One field: { type, description?, required? }. type is a non-empty string; required, when present, a boolean.
LLM-judge criteria: [{ id, name, eventName, prompt, enabled? }]. name, eventName and prompt should not be blank.
Agent Skills: named instructions the model loads on demand. Read only on version v2. Absent or []: no skill catalog, no load_skill tool, the prompt is unchanged.
Implementation version: 'v2', the current one and the reading when absent, or 'v1', deprecated, which runs the node on the legacy implementation.
Optional boolean, false when absent: whether this node's waiting execution may be resumed by an external call. Its runtime reader is not traced in workflow-core.
The name the author gives the node, e.g. 'Preguntar datos al usuario'. Every node type accepts it. A label only. No effect on execution.
Per-node non-happy-path handlers. Absent: the workspace handlers apply. Present, even empty: they replace the workspace handlers for this node.
Handler the engine runs when this node fails with no edge to follow. The only entry it looks up on non-conditional nodes.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler the engine looks up when a CONDITIONAL node fails with no edge to follow.

Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.

Completeness flag stored with the node, false on a new node. Its meaning differs between node types. No effect on execution.
Tracking events emitted after the node runs, at most 10. Each fires when enabled is true and emitOn matches the outcome.
One tracking event: its name, when it fires, an on/off switch and the payload fields.
Event name, recorded as the track name. Up to 255 characters.
false keeps the event configured but never emits it.
When the event fires: 'always' (default when absent), 'success' on a successful run, 'error' on a failed one.

Tool descriptors consumed only by the authorized runtime.

unauthorableOutlets.reason: The authoring validator accepts success, expire and failed on AI_TASK; an alert branch is rejected.

outletDocs.description: The main continuation: branch 'success' writes this edge (default type, handle the node id). The contract labels its event as waiting for initial or subsequent input.
outletDocs.fires: On the runtime event whose id is the node id. Every edge wired to it fires, in stored order; none wired parks the node.

branches.description: Where the flow goes when the AI task completes. Never 'default'.
branches.when: Always wire it (it is required on every AI_TASK). When nothing follows the AI task: a CHANNEL_MESSAGE leaf titled "Cierre"; never END without declared outputs.

outletDocs.description: The input wait expired: the node's window (settings.expiration, else the external agent cache limit) ran out. Not the same as the reminder alert.
outletDocs.fires: When the input wait expires. Every edge wired to it fires, in stored order; none wired completes the node.

branches.when: Always wire it (it is required on every AI_TASK), to a CHANNEL_MESSAGE leaf titled "Sesión expirada"; never END without declared outputs (validate --fix adds the leaf).

outletDocs.description: The expiration alert fired while the node waits. Not authorable in a workflow file: an alert branch on AI_TASK is rejected.
outletDocs.fires: When the expiration alert fires. None wired: the node stays parked.

outletDocs.description: The contract's success-typed continuation. No token writes a success-typed edge on AI_TASK (success writes the request edge), and revisions differ on falling back to default edges.
outletDocs.fires: On the node's successful continuation. Every success-typed edge fires, handles ignored, in stored order; none wired completes the node.

outletDocs.description: The node failed. The error follows the failed edge.
outletDocs.fires: When the node errors. Every failed-typed edge fires, handles ignored, in stored order; none wired completes the node.

branches.when: Only for a recovery path. For a message-only reply leave it unwired and set nonHappyPathHandlers.error; on a last AI task validate --fix folds a text-only leaf into it. Never END.

notes: With empty tools/mcp/knowledge the model can ONLY reason over upstream $memory — URLs in instructions are never fetched; decompose external data into HTTP/DATUM/CODE nodes.
Cannot route on termination status directly: pipe success → CODE (extract status) → CONDITIONAL.

An entry AI_TASK without startCommand is a blocking validate error, but the run does not stop: the engine seeds the node with the literal 'START' under the v6 system prompt, so the live symptom is a bot greeting from nowhere and ignoring the user's first message.

failed is optional — a missing failed edge is a warning, with or without a handler: failures fall through to nonHappyPathHandlers.error, else the project-level default error message, else the run ends. Wire failed only for recovery logic. Never wire failed -> END; that disables both.
There is no authorable saveResponse key: Studio's save-response control writes configuration.variable. Persisting a user reply mid-conversation is a runtime behavior of send_call_to_action.
Studio's v2 panel edits startMessage, but what persists is startCommand — author startCommand.

On expiration the turn is not simply dropped: if end_function was never called the engine runs one extraction pass over the conversation and may still write $memory.<variable>. Downstream nodes on the expire branch must tolerate a populated variable.
Every extended key here defaults to off/absent and workflows-server stores configuration as permissive pass-through, so CLI checks on them are warnings, not push blockers.
Current legacy profiles fan out every success edge; reply, exit, and successful error-events are not independently selectable.
Request, expiration, and alert handles are exact runtime event IDs.

When nothing follows the AI task: success → CHANNEL_MESSAGE leaf 'Cierre', expire → CHANNEL_MESSAGE leaf 'Sesión expirada', no failed edge (inline nonHappyPathHandlers.error), never END in a workflow without declared outputs.
Instructions are free prose; termination is configured structurally through endFunction and is never inferred from prompt headings.
Omitted, null, or empty endFunction.rawSchema uses the engine default; success and failed paths ignore handles and fan out in stored order.
Precondition: Models, tools, resources, and permissions are resolved by authorized services.

rules: Never write a START node. The tool adds the workflow's one START (`validate --fix` and `jelou push` write it), unless the workflow enters only through a WEBHOOK.
Your first edge is { "sourceId": "START", "targetId": "<first-node>", "branch": "default" }. "START" is a reserved alias the tool resolves to the real START id; no other node may use that id.
The first node cannot be START, WEBHOOK, EMPTY, NOTE.
WEBHOOK is optional, at most one per workflow, and never chained to START.

A workflow or tool that enters only through a WEBHOOK needs no START: write no edge from "START" and the tool adds none. A channel message or a TOOL node never starts it then. A marketplace skill always needs START.
Next to a wired WEBHOOK that feeds the flow, a START with no edge is only a warning: the tool wires nothing to it and push keeps it.
